paragraphs: Swamiji described Buddhism as one of the branches of India's religious family. Its founder, Gautama, grew tired of the endless metaphysical debates of his time, the heavy rituals, and above all the caste system, the idea that birth makes some people superior to others. He also opposed the enormous power of the priests.

Buddha taught a religion that asked nothing about metaphysics or theories of God. When people asked him whether God existed, he said he did not know. When they asked how to live, his answer was simple: do good and be good.

One day five Brahmins came to him to settle an argument. The first said his scripture described God in a certain way and showed a certain path to Him. The second said that was wrong: his book described God differently and taught a different path. The others did the same.

Buddha listened calmly to all of them. Then he asked each one: does your book say God gets angry, harms anyone, or is impure? No, they all agreed; every one of their books taught that God is pure and good.
Then, Buddha asked, why not first become pure and good yourselves, so that you may know what God is?
learn: Arguing about who is right can become a way to avoid actually improving. Before debating big ideas, ask what they all agree on, and start living that. Character comes first; clarity follows.
